lina: trying to onboard the new nextjs-llamaindex starter for a partner demo; ran into weird auth+retry behavior that triggers duplicate streaming calls.

owen: can you describe the flow? is this SSR or edge runtime?

lina: edge runtime (next edge). flow: user hits /api/chat which calls LlamaIndex adapter -> client.generate stream. If token expired the browser client retries, but the streaming connection starts twice and we get duplicated chunks in the console.

kevin: this sounds different from simple KV inflight dup - streaming can open two SSE/ws-like streams. Do we have idempotency in the streaming protocol?

lina: not currently. the starter uses the SDK default retry. Node SDK added idempotency for rest calls but edge client doesn't for streams.

owen: short term: add a debounce at the adapter that coalesces concurrent streams by fingerprint (prompt+model+sessionId). That should stop dup chunks for demos.

kevin: longer term, SDK parity: edge client should mirror Node's x-idempotency-key behavior and runtime should accept an idempotency header for streaming endpoints too. Also update sample README so partners know to pin token refresh strategy.

lina: filing a small e2e test for the starter: mock expired auth -> retry -> assert only one upstream stream opened. adding to tests/stream-retry.spec.ts.

ci-bot: ci: flaky evals detected: evals/llamaindex/chatstream-embed parity failing twice on branch nextjs-llamaindex-fix. Logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/evals/1757

owen: thanks. please add the CI test and I'll review the debounce PR.

lina: patch preview in starter README: "Workaround: set `sessionId` header and reuse it across retries to ensure streaming requests are coalesced by adapter."

kevin: also adding an item to SDK parity board: STREAM-IDEMPOTENCY for edge client.

lina: will send the PR with the e2e and README update shortly.
